1. (Currently amended) A method for restoring efficiency of a photovoltaic cell, the method comprising: illuminating a photovoltaic cell such that the photovoltaic cell receives a time integrated irradiance equivalent to at least 5 hours of solar illumination; and annealing the photovoltaic cell at a temperature above 90 degrees Celsius for a minimum of 10 minutes, wherein the annealing is performed after the illuminating step and in response to the illuminating step.

2. (Currently amended) The method of Claim 1, wherein the photovoltaic cell comprises a semiconductor wafer, and the method further comprises at least one of: illuminating the photovoltaic cell such that the photovoltaic cell receives a time integrated irradiance equivalent to at least 20 hours of solar illumination; illuminating the photovoltaic cell such that the photovoltaic cell receives a time integrated irradiance equivalent to at least 16 hours of solar illumination while simultaneously heating the photovoltaic cell to at least 50 degrees Celsius; and irradiating the photovoltaic cell in sunlight using a solar concentrator for at least 10 hours, wherein the solar concentrator increases the irradiance of solar illumination on the photovoltaic cell by a factor of 2 to 5.

3. (Currently amended) The method of Claim 2, wherein the photovoltaic cell is annealed at a temperature above 130 degrees Celsius, and wherein the annealing step further comprises illuminating the photovoltaic cell simultaneously with the heating.

4. (Currently amended) The method of Claim 3, wherein illuminating the photovoltaic cell during the annealing step is performed such that the photovoltaic cell receives a time integrated irradiance equivalent to at least 10 hours of solar illumination.

5. (Original) The method of Claim 1, wherein the semiconductor wafer is a silicon semiconductor wafer.

6. (Original) The method of Claim 1, wherein the photovoltaic cell is annealed at a temperature between 140 degrees Celsius and 210 degrees Celsius for a minimum of 2 hours.

7. (Original) The method of Claim 6, wherein the photovoltaic cell is a thin film photovoltaic cell.

8. (Original) The method of Claim 6, wherein the photovoltaic cell is an amorphous silicon thin film photovoltaic cell.

9. (Original) The method of claim 1, wherein the photovoltaic cell is illuminated after manufacturing of the photovoltaic cell is complete such that the photovoltaic cell produces electricity when illuminated.

10. (Original) The method of claim 1, wherein the photovoltaic cell is illuminated with a light source that simulates light from the sun.
